newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares up in strong mills, housing trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares up in strong mills, housing trade.

text.p: Active trade in the milling and housing sectors on Sunday pushed Egyptian share prices to their highest levels since March 1995, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index rose 0.21 points to close at 236.17 points with volume dropping to an average 24.72 million pounds ($7.27 million) from Thursday's 27.26 million.
"It was a good active day with a lot of work in the mills and in the housing sector, which is worth investing in," said broker Mohammed Magdi from EAB/Hermes.

The milling sector continued its domination of the bourse, with Central and West Delta Flour Mills leading the way. The stock closed 0.50 pounds higher at 60.00 after trade worth more than 2.60 million pounds.
East Delta Flour Mills traded in more than 1.60 million pounds but closed virtually unchanged at 40.01 pounds.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills jumped 2.00 pounds to close at 47.00 after trade worth more than 1.20 million pounds.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the day's most active share, dealing in more than 4.30 million pounds but the stock slipped 2.00 pounds to close at 198.
Corporate sources said on Sunday that the blue-chip realty firm will give out a 10 pound dividend for financial 1995/96 compared to 6.90 pounds in the previous finanical year.

They said the firm, one of the state's most successful privatisations, would give out the dividend on November 14 but quashed rumours that it would also distribute a free share with the cash dividend.
Investors scooped up Medinet Nasr shares last week after the free share talk flooded the market.
The realty firm said in results made available on Sunday it raised net distributable profits for 1995/96 by 43 percent to 52.21 million from 36.53 million a year earlier.
Heliopolis Housing and Development traded in more than 78,000 pounds but it slipped 2.00 pounds to close at 188.

The cement sector began to pick up after a recent slow spate. Helwan Portland Cement rose 0.10 pounds to close at 50.00 after trade worth more than 1.30 million pounds and Suez Cement closed 0.16 pounds higher at 48.25 after trade worth almost a million pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 345.56 points from Thursday's 345.22 and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 168.92 from 168.79 points.
